I understand Spanish, but I can't speak it. It's not a talent problem

You understand Spanish, but your mind goes blank when you speak. It's not a lack of talent: you trained recognition for years, not speaking.

Published November 17, 2026 · 6 min read · Sławomir Onyszko

You know this feeling.

You understand Spanish: series without subtitles, articles without a dictionary, a client email without panic. Then a moment arrives when you have to say something. Your mind goes blank. You know what you want to say, but in Spanish you say "eh" or the safe "sí, sí, claro". The more important the conversation, the fewer words arrive. A job interview, a client call, a conversation with your partner's family. Everything you know suddenly disappears.

If you explain this to yourself as a lack of talent, age, or "that's just how I am", here is good news. It is not a talent problem. It is the result of a method that trained something other than speaking with you for years.

Recognition and speaking are two different skills

You recognize a song after two chords. Now sing it exactly, with the lyrics, in time. That is harder than it sounds. Language works the same way. Recognition and speaking your own sentences are two different skills.

  • Recognition: you see or hear a sentence and know what it means. You can pick the correct answer out of four.
  • Speaking your own sentences: you build your own sentence and say it out loud. Alone, without hints, under time pressure.

You can recognize aunque when you read it. That does not mean you can say Aunque estaba cansado, terminé la lección without pausing. You can know that Soy 30 años is wrong. That does not mean that under pressure you will say Tengo 30 años. Recognition gives you the answer. Speaking asks you to build it yourself, from memory, in real time.

School and apps trained recognition with you for years. Multiple choice, quizzes, matching pairs, fill in the gap. Every one of those exercises asks your brain one question: "Do you recognize this?" None asks: "Can you say something of your own?" Speaking grows only when you have to say something of your own.

You freeze because nobody trained speaking with you

If the method trained recognition for twelve years, you have recognition. Speaking does not appear by itself. The skill you need in a work conversation was simply never trained.

It is not a talent problem. It is a training plan that never existed. Nobody asked you to build your own sentence and say it out loud every day. Nobody corrected you right after you said it. Nobody brought your mistakes back a few days later. So your brain had no reason to train that skill.

School and apps are not bad tools. They are good tools for a different job. They give you words, grammar and understanding. That is a necessary foundation. But a foundation is not a house. Understanding is not speaking.

You are not alone

On language-learning forums the same motif returns every week:

  • I click through an app for half an hour a day for six months, I finished the course, and I still can't speak.
  • I have a 1500-day streak in an app, and conversation still doesn't work.
  • Everyone sells fluency in 3 months, and people after years of study can't say a sentence.

You are not the only one. The same story shows up on forums again and again, for people who learned in school, in apps and on courses. The streak grows, the points grow, the app level grows. Speaking does not grow, because nobody ever had to say anything and correct it.

If you thought the problem was you, here is the better explanation. The problem is the method, which did not include speaking practice.

Waiting has a cost

Time does not fix this. Time deepens it:

  • Passive vocabulary, the words you recognize but do not use, fades without contact. Understanding you never use gets weaker.
  • Every situation where you lack words adds another layer of fear. Next year it will be the same, only with higher stakes: a new job, a move abroad, a client call.
  • The habit of silence gets stronger. The longer you avoid speaking, the harder it is to start.

I am not saying this to scare you. It is ordinary math: every month without speaking is a month in which that skill does not grow. And the opportunities you are preparing for will not wait until you feel ready.

Speaking is built from three things

Speaking is a skill, so it grows through practice that trains it directly. Every day you need three things:

  1. Speaking your own sentences. You build your own sentences, say them and write them. You do not pick answers from a list. You do not read a prepared dialogue. You talk about your day, your work, your plans.
  2. A specific correction. Someone tells you what you said, what it should sound like and why. Not good, almost, but you said X, it should be Y, because Z. The correction can come from a tutor, a language exchange partner or an app. The first session does not need a correction. A correction is the next step.
  3. Spaced review. The system brings back what is starting to fade, exactly when it is needed. You do not have to remember when to review a word. Something asks you at the right moment.

That is how you practice piano. Swimming works the same way: time in the water, not theory on the shore. Language is no exception.

Start with 3 sentences

For today, without any app and without any course: tonight, say 3 sentences about your day out loud. Say them in Spanish. For example: Hoy me desperté a las siete. Hice café. Tengo una reunión a las diez. Nobody is listening, so a mistake costs nothing.

This can be your first practice in speaking your own sentences. It will take 2 minutes. If you want, record yourself and listen once. You will hear where you stop and which word is missing. That is not a correction yet. It is an observation, and it is where the work starts. 3 sentences will not fix all of speaking. It is a first step, not the whole method.

Let me know how it went.

Soliloquy exists to make that work daily. But today's task does not need an app. 3 sentences and 2 minutes of courage are enough.
